name: Example · Website launch
description: A fictional, editable project to explore Kanban and Mind Map. Includes three task levels, rich specs, dates, blockers and four example assignees.

tasks.title: Discover the opportunity
tasks.outcome: Agree who the website is for and what a successful launch should achieve.
acceptance: Identify the primary audience and their top needs
Record measurable launch outcomes and the agreed scope

tasks.title: Interview the audience
tasks.outcome: Capture a short research brief from five fictional customer interviews.
acceptance: Summarise the recurring needs and frustrations
Share a one-page findings note with the project team

tasks.title: Agree the project brief
tasks.outcome: Turn research findings into a clear problem statement, scope and delivery brief.
acceptance: Record the included pages and explicitly excluded work
Agree the delivery milestones and review owners

tasks.title: Audit the existing content
tasks.outcome: Create an inventory of existing pages and decide what to retain, rewrite or retire.
acceptance: Assign a disposition to every page in the example inventory
Identify content gaps and the owner of each rewrite

tasks.title: Design a welcoming experience
tasks.outcome: Design a clear, accessible path from the landing page to a confident enquiry.
acceptance: Review the information architecture with the team
Approve the desktop and mobile prototype before hand-off

tasks.title: Map the visitor journeys
tasks.outcome: Map the two primary visitor journeys and the navigation structure.
acceptance: Show the path from landing to enquiry
Ensure every primary page has a clear next action

tasks.title: Create the interactive prototype
tasks.outcome: Build an interactive design prototype covering the landing, product and contact pages.
acceptance: Include realistic empty, loading and validation states
Capture review feedback next to the relevant screen

tasks.title: Check the mobile layout
tasks.outcome: Review how the proposed screens adapt to narrow widths and touch input.
acceptance: Keep headings, actions and form fields readable at narrow widths
Check that sticky elements do not obscure content

tasks.title: Review the prototype with the team
tasks.outcome: Walk through the prototype together and resolve the remaining design decisions.
acceptance: Record decisions and assign owners to follow-ups
Approve the interactions needed for implementation

tasks.title: Write the content voice guide
tasks.outcome: Define a friendly, direct writing style. This task is intentionally overdue so the date treatment is visible.
acceptance: Include examples for headings, buttons and error messages
Agree how product terminology should be used consistently

tasks.title: Build the new website
tasks.outcome: Implement the approved experience and connect the content and enquiry flows.
acceptance: Build reusable page sections from the approved design
Keep configuration and content separate from presentation code

tasks.title: Set up the application foundation
tasks.outcome: Prepare the application structure, shared styles and local development workflow.
acceptance: Document the local startup and build commands
Make a minimal end-to-end page work before expanding it

tasks.title: Implement the core pages
tasks.outcome: Build the landing, product and contact pages using the agreed content and components.
acceptance: Match the approved layout at desktop and mobile widths
Keep page content editable through the established content path

tasks.title: Connect the enquiry form
tasks.outcome: Implement clear validation, confirmation and failure recovery for enquiries.
acceptance: Show helpful field-level validation messages
Do not report a successful enquiry until delivery is confirmed

tasks.title: Define the launch measurement plan
tasks.outcome: Define which events will answer the agreed launch questions. No live tracking is enabled by this example.
acceptance: Map each launch outcome to a clear event definition
Document consent and data-minimisation requirements for later review

tasks.title: Make it ready for people
tasks.outcome: Review the complete experience for usability, accessibility and reliability.
acceptance: Resolve release-blocking defects against the agreed acceptance checks
Record the tested browser and device coverage

tasks.title: Run the accessibility review
tasks.outcome: Review keyboard access, focus order, text contrast and form feedback.
acceptance: Complete the primary journeys using only the keyboard
Record automated findings and verify the important paths manually

tasks.title: Test the browser and device journeys
tasks.outcome: Test navigation and enquiry handling across the supported browsers and representative screen sizes.
acceptance: Capture the actual browser and device versions tested
Check slow loading, failed requests and retry behaviour

tasks.title: Resolve the release blockers
tasks.outcome: Triage the review findings and fix the issues that block a confident release.
acceptance: Give each blocking issue a clear reproduction and owner
Retest the original failing scenario after each fix

tasks.title: Launch and learn
tasks.outcome: Plan a controlled launch, review the first feedback and capture what comes next.
acceptance: Agree the release checklist and recovery plan
Schedule a short learning review after launch

tasks.title: Prepare the launch checklist
tasks.outcome: Write the release steps and define the signals that would trigger a rollback.
acceptance: Identify who makes the release decision
Record the verification and recovery steps in order

tasks.title: Review and publish the release
tasks.outcome: A fictional milestone for trying dependencies. This example does not deploy or publish any website.
acceptance: Complete the release-readiness review
Verify the intended experience after the simulated release

tasks.title: Capture the first-week learnings
tasks.outcome: Compare the first feedback with the original goals and shape the next iteration.
acceptance: Summarise the important observations without inventing results
Create follow-up tasks for the next improvement cycle
